content.content:
Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

Blake

input.description: Scan ZOM comments for tiers notes
input.prompt:
Read-only research task. Do NOT write/comment/modify anything. Use the Linear MCP tools (mcp__hg__linear_list_issues, mcp__hg__linear_list_comments).

Goal: In Linear team ZOM ("Zombie Match 3D"), go through EVERY issue created on or before 2025-08-31 (issue numbers roughly ZOM-10 to ~ZOM-520; list them with mcp__hg__linear_list_issues team=ZOM, includeArchived=true, orderBy=createdAt, limit=250, paginate with cursor; filter createdAt <= 2025-08-31T23:59:59Z). For each issue, call mcp__hg__linear_list_comments (limit 250) and read every comment.

Report back, verbatim, every comment that:
1. starts with "tiers:" (case-insensitive, possibly with leading whitespace) — include issue id, issue title, issue status, comment author, date, full text.
2. contains "not tiers" — same details.
3. says the ticket replaces / supersedes another ticket (e.g. "replaces ZOM-123", "supersedes", "replaced by") — same details.
Also report any comment by Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co / "Blake") that looks like a closing note on these tickets regardless of wording if it mentions tier, difficulty, enrage, CPM or blunder.

Be exhaustive — don't skip issues. At the end, state how many issues you checked and the id range covered. Return a compact list.

content.content: {"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this \\\"early exit\\\" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.\\n2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.\\n\\nPlease note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.\\n\\nThis also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.\\n\\nA losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.\\n\\n# **Part 2: Future expansion**\\n\\nIf a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:\\n\\nMonster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with\\n\\nPunk A | Punk B\\n\\nPunk B | Punk C\\n\\nPunk C | Punk D\\n\\nPunk D | Brute A\\n\\nBoss 1 | Boss 3\\n\\nBoss 2 | Boss 4\\n\\nBoss 10 | Boss 10\\n\\nIf the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.\\n\\nThe other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster \\\"rank\\\" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the \\\"next rank\\\" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:\\nPunk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C\\n\\nThen Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.\\n\\nThis will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.\", \"priority\": {\"value\": 1, \"name\": \"Urgent\"}, \"estimate\": null, \"url\": \"https://linear.app/harmonygames/issue/ZOM-42/dynamic-difficulty\", \"gitBranchName\": \"julialawson/zom-42-dynamic-difficulty\", \"createdAt\": \"2025-04-21T16:28:42Z\", \"updatedAt\": \"2025-05-31T02:54:30Z\", \"archivedAt\": null, \"completedAt\": \"2025-05-30T22:06:46Z\", \"startedAt\": \"2025-05-23T15:05:35Z\", \"canceledAt\": null, \"dueDate\": null, \"status\": \"Done\", \"statusType\": \"completed\", \"labels\": [\"Level Editor\", \"Backend Engineering\"], \"links\": [], \"attachments\": [], \"createdBy\": \"Robert\", \"createdById\": \"usr_Robert\", \"assignee\": \"arthur.blake@harmonygames.co\", \"assigneeId\": \"usr_cc3e90160f490686\", \"project\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"projectId\": \"dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624\", \"team\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"teamId\": \"team_ZOM\", \"timeInStatusMinutes\": 177656, \"isArchived\": false, \"stateHistory\": []}"}

{"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

Then Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.

This will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. \\nZOM-303 Dynamic Difficult Design Oversight Fix\\n

\\n\\nCurrently, the players advances a tier whenever they win 8 out of last 10 games.\\n\\nThis means by level 40, a player can easily be labeled as tier 4, which is often the case given how easy our game is early on.\\n\\nHowever many of our levels only have 2 tiers of difficult, 0 and 1. And the idea is that if a player loses 4 in a row, they get demoted a player tier. So 4 -> 3 -> 2 and -> 1. However this creates a problem.\\n\\nA player is difficulty tier 4, plays a difficulty tier 1 level, gets stuck, loses 4 in a row, they are demoted to tier 3. They still load difficulty tier 1 level, and continues to lose. A player would need to lose 12 times for them to actually get to difficulty tier 0 for that level. This defeats the whole purpose of downgrading them. Losing 12 in a row will cause a user to churn.\\n\\nSolution: when a player is demoted, we also need to demote the level difficulty for the level they are currently on.\\n\\nSo if a player is demoted from tier 4 -> 3, and they were playing tier 1 difficulty and failed, that level will load the tier 0 version.\\n\\nThe following level, it will just go back to normal, meaning if a tier 3 level is available, that's the level that will load for the player. Otherwise we load the tier difficulty closes to the player's current tier.\\n

\\n

values: How it works in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133)

Every player starts on tier 0. The starting-tier check runs when a player's 10th game ends (wins and losses both count, not 10 levels cleared): average CPM > 90 moves them to tier 1, everyone else stays on tier 0. 90 exactly stays on tier 0.
The build, per Blake's reply to the store builds mail (Sep 30). ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels; the build never changed from the original spec.

Tier -2 is an exception: you promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate up to the most recent 10 attempts of the player and promote if win rate is 80% or higher (early exit: winning 8 in a row promotes without playing the full 10). Every promotion/demotion resets the record to 0 games played.

Lose 4 in a row and you're demoted; this can trigger at any time regardless of the record. Separately, we demote when win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower (early exits possible, e.g. LLLWLL). Every promotion/demotion resets the record to 0 games played. 60-70% win rate: no change.
Does the level drop after a demotion?
Yes. When a player is demoted on a level, that level loads one tier lower on the retry; the next level goes back to the player's tier (or the closest tier the level has).
ZOM-303 (Live, match3d#244). Note: ZOM-293 'Dynamic Difficulty Tiering Down Issue' is still open (Todo).
A blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages the monsters on the board. Enrage adds walk speed and attack damage only; the HP part is switched off.
ZOM-282, which replaced the ZOM-254 blunder 2.0 boost (Robert's deck still shows +25% HP).
Per monster, copied as it stands from the Live tab of the ZM monster enrage sheet (below).

content.text:
I've built the register, shared it, left the ticket comments his rules called for, and replied to Leonard in his DM thread ([message](https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/D05HB64NMQU/p1759302503000000?thread_ts=1759261706.530914&cid=D05HB64NMQU)).

**The register:** it's a sheet called "ZM difficulty baseline - Oct 6" in the ZM Difficulty folder ([link](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/4fa2058b1dc341c8/edit)). It has the two tabs from the session agenda, Tickets and Rules in force.
- **Columns:** the ones the Trello card asks for, plus the three Robert wanted in your group chat (Linear assignee, done date in Pacific time, priority).
- **Statuses:** judged against the two store builds Blake named, iOS 0.3.49 and Android 0.3.133.
- **Enrage numbers:** copied exactly from the Live tab of your monster enrage sheet. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl show "not copied yet", as they do there.

**What made the list:** 22 tickets.

| Status | Count | Tickets |
|---|---|---|
| Live | 14 | |
| Editor only | 4 | ZOM-173, 200, 277, 315 |
| Replaced | 1 | ZOM-254, replaced by ZOM-282 |
| Not shipped | 3 | ZOM-202, 280, 293 |

- **Added:** ZOM-221, 300, 305 and 378 don't match the title keywords, but they're on because Blake's closing notes start with "tiers:".
- **Taken off:** ZOM-295 and ZOM-312 match the keywords, but Blake marked both "not tiers" on their PRs. Also off are everything Leonard excluded across his DM and notes doc (30, 49, 50, 161, 162, 163, 201, 250, 258, 262, 275) and the duplicates (203, 276).

**When a new player gets their starting tier:** when their 10th game ends, counting wins and losses, not after 10 levels cleared. An average CPM above 90 moves them to tier 1, and exactly 90 stays on tier 0. That's what Blake says the build does; ZOM-199 and Robert's deck both say "90 or more after 10 levels".

**Sharing:** Robert can edit, Leonard and Brian can comment, and Arthur can only view.
- **Brian:** the Trello checklist says to give him edit, but Leonard's later DM overrides that.
- **Arthur:** the card says everyone else comments, but Leonard's notes doc says view is enough since he's only listening in.

**Ticket comments (9 in total):**
- **ZOM-199:** what the build actually does.
- **ZOM-254:** that ZOM-282 replaced it.
- **The 7 Editor only and Not shipped tickets:** a note that the change isn't in the store builds, naming both builds.

No other tickets were touched, and none of 162, 163, 201 or 250 got a comment.

**Search gap:** I searched for Blake's "tiers:" notes and "not tiers" reviews only on Blake-assigned tickets and on the PRs linked to the shortlisted tickets. The helper agents I started for a wider search kept running out of memory. A "tiers:" note on a ticket assigned to someone else, or a "not tiers" review on an unlinked PR, would have been missed.

**Judgement calls:**
- **ZOM-263:** marked Live with no PR checked. It's a fix to the attack power formula and I assumed it's the in-game number.
- **ZOM-45:** marked Live because Blake's note says the game reads the label at runtime.
- **Level drop after a demotion:** the rules tab says yes, the current level loads one tier lower on retry (from ZOM-303). It also notes that ZOM-293, a related bug about tiering down, is still open.
